A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of a high-grade lesion, a large lesion size, and an extensive margin were associated with a significantly increased risk of local recurrence after excision alone for DCIS.

the presence of comedo necrosis in the excised specimen, the presence of a positive surgical margin, the size of the tumor, the age of the patient, and the presence of lymph node metastases are the most significant predictors of local recurrence following treatment of DCIS with excision alone.
the presence of comedo necrosis in DCIS is associated with increased local recurrence following excison alone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a subset of patients who have a low rate of local recurrence after excision alone and that we can identify those patients by looking at a number of clinical factors.
patients with DCIS who have a low-risk lesion (low nuclear grade, low Ki67, low comedo necrosis), and who have negative margins, can be treated with excision only, without the use of radiation.
patients with low-grade DCIS, negative margins, no comedo-necrosis, and small tumors are unlikely to have a local recurrence after excision alone.
